title: India Ranks 13th Among World's Best Cuisines in TasteAtlas Awards
excerpt: Butter garlic naan and Amritsari kulcha lead Indian entries, with Mumbai named among the world's top five food cities in the annual global food rankings.
body:
• India secured the 13th position in TasteAtlas's 100 Best Cuisines in the World for 2025-26, with a score of 4.43 out of 5.
  • Butter garlic naan and Amritsari kulcha, both rated 4.7, are India's highest-scored dishes globally.
  • Mumbai was named among the world's top five food cities, while Punjab ranked 7th among the best food regions worldwide.
  • The rankings are based on 590,228 validated ratings across 18,912 dishes cataloged by the Croatian food guide.

Indian cuisine has claimed the 13th spot in the TasteAtlas Awards 2025-26 list of the 100 Best Cuisines in the World, with butter garlic naan and Amritsari kulcha leading India's entries as the country's highest-rated dishes globally.

The annual ranking by the Croatian experiential food guide, based on 590,228 validated ratings across 18,912 dishes worldwide, gave Indian cuisine an overall score of 4.43 out of 5. Italy topped the list at 4.64, followed by Greece at 4.60 and Peru at 4.54.

India's Star Dishes

Two Indian breads dominated the country's entries. Butter garlic naan scored 4.53 on the global dishes list, ranking among the world's top breads, while Amritsari kulcha matched it at 4.44. Other must-try Indian dishes highlighted by TasteAtlas include Hyderabadi biryani, murgh makhani (butter chicken), garam masala, parotta, and muthia.

In the stews category, India punched above its weight with 15 entries in the top 100, including murgh makhani at 4th, shahi paneer at 6th, and keema at 23rd.

"Indian food is more than just spice and aroma — it's a tapestry woven from centuries of migration, royal influence, regional produce, and cultural rituals."

— TasteAtlas editorial assessment

Mumbai Shines, Punjab Surprises

In companion rankings, Mumbai was named among the world's top five food cities — the only Indian metropolis in the top 10. The city's street food culture, spanning vada pav, pav bhaji, and chaat, alongside its growing fine-dining scene, earned global recognition. Amritsar ranked 48th, while New Delhi and Hyderabad placed 53rd and 54th respectively.

Punjab emerged as a surprise standout, ranking 7th globally among the best food regions — ahead of destinations like Tuscany and Andalusia. Southern India also featured at 40th, with West Bengal, Maharashtra, and Kerala making the top 100.

Iconic Restaurants Win Recognition

Several Indian restaurants earned spots on the iconic traditional restaurants list. Dum Pukht in New Delhi, Ram Ashraya in Mumbai, Shree Thaker Bhojanalay in Mumbai, Nawab Saheb in Mumbai, and Suvarna Mahal in Jaipur were all highlighted. Paragon Restaurant in Kozhikode and Peter Cat in Kolkata featured prominently in earlier TasteAtlas rankings as well.

India's gourmet producers also gained attention, with Eleftheria Cheese, Amrut Distilleries, Godawan spirits, Manam Chocolate, and Under The Mango Tree bee products all receiving recognition.

Global Culinary Competition

The top 15 cuisines in the 2025-26 ranking are: Italy, Greece, Peru, Portugal, Spain, Japan, Turkey, China, France, Indonesia, Mexico, Serbia, India, Poland, and the United States. India outranked American cuisine for the second consecutive year and continues to surpass Thai, South Korean, and German food in global ratings.

The rankings reflect aggregated user ratings validated against editorial standards, though critics note they can skew toward dishes familiar to Western palates. Regional specialties from India's northeast and tribal cuisines remain underrepresented in global food databases.

What It Means for Indian Food Globally

For the Indian diaspora, the ranking affirms what millions already know: Indian food has achieved permanent global status. Indian restaurants now rank among the best in cities from London to Singapore, and chefs like Vikas Khanna — recently named to TIME's 100 Most Influential People list for 2026 — continue to raise the cuisine's international profile.
nri_angle: The TasteAtlas ranking validates Indian cuisine's global standing, resonating with diaspora communities who have long championed their food traditions abroad.
